questions.q: What is Nsight Systems best suited for?
options: Deep per-kernel hardware-counter analysis of a single kernel
Tracing a whole application's timeline across CPU, GPU, and memory activity to find where time is going
Editing CUDA source code
Managing GPU driver installations
questions.explain: Nsight Systems gives a system-wide timeline view, ideal for spotting idle gaps, unnecessary synchronization, and where time is actually spent across a whole run.

questions.q: What does Nsight Compute provide that Nsight Systems does not?
options: A system-wide CPU/GPU timeline
Deep, per-kernel hardware-counter metrics like achieved occupancy, DRAM throughput, and the specific limiter holding that kernel back
The ability to edit a model's architecture
Real-time power management controls
questions.explain: Nsight Compute profiles one kernel in isolation with full hardware-counter detail, identifying exactly which resource is limiting that specific kernel.

questions.q: Why is the typical workflow 'Nsight Systems first, Nsight Compute second'?
options: Nsight Compute cannot run without a prior Nsight Systems trace

Nsight Systems triages where time is going across the whole app; Nsight Compute's deep instrumentation is too expensive to run on every kernel, so you target it at the few kernels Nsight Systems flagged
Nsight Systems must be uninstalled before running Nsight Compute
They produce identical reports, so order doesn't matter
questions.explain: Nsight Systems' broad timeline helps identify which kernels are worth investigating, since Nsight Compute's per-kernel instrumentation overhead makes profiling every kernel impractical.

questions.q: In an Nsight Compute report, what does the 'limiter' (or speed-of-light metric) tell you?
options: The maximum clock speed the GPU can reach
Which resource — compute throughput or memory throughput — is actually capping that kernel's performance
How many lines of source code the kernel has
The GPU driver version in use
questions.explain: The limiter metric directly identifies whether a kernel is compute-bound or memory-bound, based on measured hardware counters rather than estimation.

questions.q: What is an NVTX marker used for?
options: A custom-named range added to application code so it appears labeled in the Nsight Systems timeline
A hardware register that stores GPU temperature
A CUDA compiler optimization flag
A type of memory transaction
questions.explain: NVTX markers let developers annotate custom ranges (like 'forward pass' or 'data loading') so they show up clearly labeled in an Nsight Systems timeline trace.
